_design: ONE model, trained ONCE on the pooled training datasets of every family, then
evaluated on each family's held-out dataset (100% of its *test.csv files).
Per family, the higher-content dataset(s) go into the shared TRAIN pool and the
remaining one is held out. So every held-out dataset has at least one same-family
sibling in the training pool, and contributes zero training windows itself.
TRAIN pool (9) : MITDB, SMAP, Exathlon, SMD, Daphnet, GHL, GECCO, metro, room-occupancy
HELD OUT   (6) : SVDB,  MSL, PSM,           OPPORTUNITY, Genesis, CalIt2
This is F2A's protocol (one jointly fine-tuned model, evaluated on datasets excluded
from training) with the confound removed: F2A's held-out set mixes datasets that DID
have a same-family sibling in training (Daphnet, PSM, Genesis, SWaT) with one that did
NOT (CreditCard), and never varies it. Here sibling coverage is guaranteed by design.
TRADE-OFF, state it in the writeup: a single pooled model cannot attribute a gain on
SVDB to MITDB specifically -- the model also saw SMAP, SMD, GHL and the rest. It
answers 'does a family-sibling-covered pool transfer to unseen datasets', not 'which
sibling did the work'. Per-family attribution needs one model per family (6 runs);
the machinery supports it via  bash make_folds.py --per_family.
tier 1 = defensible. tier 2 = UNDERPOWERED, report separately (see 'caveat').

ecg.note: Both 2-lead ECG, F=3, ~13% anomalous, same anomaly semantics (arrhythmic beats). The flagship.

spacecraft.note: Both NASA telemetry. F differs (SMAP 26 / MSL 56); most channels are one-hot command flags.

server.note: Only 3-dataset family. PSM held out: 1 file, anomaly-dense (32%), so VUS-PR is well conditioned.

activity.note: Same sensor modality (body-worn IMU) but DIFFERENT anomaly semantics (freezing-of-gait vs activity transition). A null result here is ambiguous between domain mismatch and label mismatch.

industrial.caveat: Genesis has ~28 anomalous timesteps TOTAL (0.30% of 9332). VUS-PR is noise-dominated; a bad number does NOT mean transfer failed.
industrial.note: Reverse direction (train on Genesis) is not viable -- far too few anomaly windows.

env_iot.caveat: CalIt2 test set is 55 windows / ~138 anomalous timesteps; metro in the train pool has ~31. Measured, not estimated.
env_iot.note: Weakest grouping: water quality vs freeway traffic vs room CO2 vs building door counts is 'has sensors', not one domain.

excluded_singletons._comment: One-dataset families -- no sibling, so same-family transfer is undefined. Excluded from BOTH pool and held-out set.
